draft.change: Extend the existing this-one sense to cover forward reference and cite Gen.6.15.
draft.definition: Used independently, זֶה can introduce what the speaker is about to specify.
draft.evidence: In Gen.6.15 the three measurements following וְזֶה אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה אֹתָהּ supply the content of ‘this’.

patch.value: Root question: no verbal or nominal root was found. The word is the Semitic pointing (deictic) element *ḏ-, with vowel endings for gender and case (Arabic ḏā, ḏī, ḏū; Ugaritic d/ḏ, f. dt; Sabaic ḏ-, ḏn; Ge'ez zə, za; Aramaic dā, dī, dənā; Phoenician z, zn), found in every branch; scripture has no noun or verb זהה/זוה/זיה from which it could have grown, and Arabic grammarians' reconstructions of ذَا as ذَوَى or ذَيَى (Lane p. 947) only fit it to the root pattern. The later Hebrew verb זִהָה "identify" is formed from זֶה, not the reverse. So the entry is keyed by its own consonants, זה, and the evidence for the pointing word itself is as strong as for any Semitic word. One pointer serves as demonstrative and relative across the languages (Hebrew זוּ and poetic זֶה, Aramaic דִּי, Ugaritic d, Sabaic ḏ-, Ge'ez za, Old Byblian z, Arabic ḏū in Ṭayyiʾ), which is why the relative words are kept here. Not this element: Hebrew שֶׁ־ and Akkadian ša (Akkadian keeps ḏ as z, so ša does not answer to ḏ; Wiktionary's comparison of ša with ذَا is not followed); אֵלֶּה "these" and Aramaic אִלֵּין (another pointing word, ʾl); Syriac ܗܳܢܳܐ "this" (hn); the month name זִו (זיו "brightness"). BDB files זֹאת under זֶה (g.ah.aa); its cross-reference key g.ab.ad has no tokens and is claimed here. g.ai.aa and g.aj.aa list the same two tokens of זוֹ (Hos 7:16, Psa 132:12); both keys are on זֹה, so they are counted twice there. Zec 2:8 and Psa 68:9 are cited by the Hebrew numbering (English 2:4, 68:8); Dan 4:14, 4:22, 4:27, 6:11 and 4:29 likewise (English 4:17, 4:25, 4:30, 6:10 and 4:32). Not consulted: CAL (refuses automated access), DULAT, Leslau, Old Aramaic inscriptions (znh, zy). Dillmann's column numbers were read from the Internet Archive OCR and should be checked on the page image. זֶה סִינַי is left open between a title ("the One of Sinai") and "this Sinai". The particle's senses are illustrative, not exhaustive: about 1,800 tokens.

Stands alone for someone or something present or just spoken of, or points forward to what the speaker is about to specify. It often serves as the subject of a clause with no verb, “this is …”. The feminine זֹאת stands for a matter, a deed or a word as a whole, where English says “this” or “it”.
וְזֶה אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה אֹתָהּ means ‘and this is how you shall make it.’ The dimensions that follow specify what זֶה points to.
זֶה־שְּׁמִי לְעֹלָם וְזֶה זִכְרִי לְדֹר דֹּר: "this is my name for ever, and this my memorial to generation after generation".
מֵאֵת יַהְוֶה הָיְתָה זֹּאת: "from Yahweh this came about"; the Greek keeps the feminine, αὕτη (Mat 21:42).
כִּי זֹאת הַבְּרִית אֲשֶׁר אֶכְרֹת: "for this is the covenant that I will cut"; quoted at Heb 8:10.

value.note: אֵין זֶה כִּי אִם־בֵּית אֱלֹהִים וְזֶה שַׁעַר הַשָּׁמָיִם: "this is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven".

analysis.evidence: וְזֶה אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה אֹתָהּ means ‘and this is how you shall make it.’ The feminine object אֹתָהּ refers to the ark. זֶה points forward to its prescribed length, width, and height, given as 300, 50, and 30 cubits.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed conjunction וְ ‘and’ + independent masculine singular demonstrative pronoun זֶה.
analysis.sense: This, pointing forward to the specifications about to be given.

analysis.evidence: In וְזֶה אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה אֹתָהּ («and this is how you shall make it»), אֲשֶׁר introduces a relative clause modifying זֶה. The object אֹתָהּ refers to the ark, and the dimensions that follow specify how it is to be made.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected relative particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The feminine singular object pronoun אֹתָהּ refers to הַתֵּבָה, the ark. Its length, width, and height specify how Noah is to build it.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, second masculine singular, with directive force

analysis.evidence: שְׁלֹשׁ counts מֵאוֹת ‘hundreds’. Together, שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת אַמָּה gives the ark’s length as three hundred cubits. The reduced first vowel in שְׁלֹשׁ marks the construct form of שָׁלֹשׁ.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular cardinal numeral in the construct state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת אַמָּה, שְׁלֹשׁ counts three hundreds, and אַמָּה supplies the unit. The phrase gives the ark’s length as three hundred cubits.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, plural absolute, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: hundreds (plural מֵאוֹת, with the digits: three hundred to nine hundred)

analysis.evidence: שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת אַמָּה gives the ark’s length (אֹרֶךְ הַתֵּבָה) as three hundred cubits. The singular אַמָּה names the unit of length, which English renders in the plural after three hundred.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֹרֶךְ הַתֵּבָה means “the length of the ark.” The verse gives that dimension as three hundred cubits, alongside fifty cubits for its width and thirty for its height.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular construct, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֹרֶךְ הַתֵּבָה means “the length of the ark.” The verse gives its length as 300 cubits. The feminine singular suffixes in רָחְבָּהּ “its width” and קוֹמָתָהּ “its height” refer to the same vessel and give its other dimensions.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a feminine singular common noun in the absolute state.
analysis.sense: The vessel built by Noah to carry people and animals through the flood.

analysis.evidence: In חֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה רָחְבָּהּ, “fifty cubits is its width,” the numeral counts cubits across the ark. The parallel measurements give its length as three hundred cubits and its height as thirty.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, common gender, plural absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In חֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה רָחְבָּהּ, “its width is fifty cubits,” the singular noun אַמָּה gives the unit of measure for the ark’s width.
חֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה רָחְבָּהּ gives the ark’s width as fifty cubits, between its length of three hundred cubits and its height of thirty cubits.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with a third-person feminine singular possessive suffix ־ָהּ referring to הַתֵּבָה, the ark.

analysis.evidence: וּשְׁלֹשִׁים אַמָּה קוֹמָתָהּ means “and its height was thirty cubits.” The numeral gives the ark’s height, and וּ joins this measurement to the preceding width.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ prefixed to a cardinal numeral, plural absolute, used with either gender.

analysis.evidence: In וּשְׁלֹשִׁים אַמָּה קוֹמָתָהּ, “and its height was thirty cubits,” אַמָּה supplies the unit for the ark’s height, just as it does for its length and width earlier in the verse.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The verse gives the ark’s length, then its width, then its height. In וּשְׁלֹשִׁים אַמָּה קוֹמָתָהּ, the final measurement is thirty cubits, and the suffix ־ָהּ refers to הַתֵּבָה, the ark.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular noun in the construct state with a third-person feminine singular possessive suffix referring to the ark.
